chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn al-Mukhtār, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: “If there were stoppers for your tongues, I would tell every person what is for him and what is against him.”

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Muḥammad al-Bāqir (عليه السلام), the speaker of the hadith
key_terms.أَلْسِنَتِكُمْ: your tongues; a reference to speech and the failure to restrain it
key_terms.أَوْكِيَةٌ: stoppers or bindings; metaphorically, restraints that prevent disclosure
key_terms.بِمَا لَهُ وَعَلَيْهِ: that which is in his favor and that which is against him
key_terms.لَحَدَّثْتُ: I would have narrated or informed

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) say he would inform every person of what was for and against him if tongues were restrained?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Imam (عليه السلام) possessed knowledge concerning each person's condition, but withheld disclosing it because people did not reliably guard what they heard. Its significance lies in showing both the special knowledge of the Imam and the ethical necessity of restraint and trustworthiness in receiving sensitive truths.
